components.name: Button
components.description: A clickable control that triggers an action — submitting a form, confirming a decision, or opening a dialog. It comes in six emphasis variants across three sizes, supports optional leading and trailing icons and a loading state, and binds every color, spacing, radius, and type value to the system's semantic tokens.
whenToUse: Trigger an action or event — submit, confirm, open a dialog
Give a view a single, clear primary action
whenNotToUse: Navigating to another page or URL — use a Link (the link variant looks like a link but still triggers an action)

variant.default: Highest-emphasis, solid brand fill — the one primary action in a view.
variant.secondary: Medium-emphasis, muted fill — sits alongside a primary action.
variant.destructive: Solid danger fill — irreversible or destructive actions such as delete.
variant.outline: Bordered with a transparent fill — low emphasis that still needs a visible edge.
variant.ghost: No fill until hover — lowest emphasis, for toolbars and dense UI.
variant.link: Styled as an inline text link — least chrome.

states.hover: Pointer over the button — fill shifts to the hover token.
states.focus: Keyboard focus — shows the focus ring (neutral ring, or the on-fill ring over solid variants).
states.disabled: Non-interactive and not focusable; reduced opacity.
states.loading: Shows a spinner in place of the leading icon and disables the button until the action resolves.

dos: Lead the label with a verb
Keep one primary (default) button per view
Keep labels short — about three words or fewer
donts: Don't use a button for navigation — use a Link
Don't stack multiple primary buttons in one view
Don't disable a button without telling the user why

notes: Renders a native <button>, so role="button" is implicit
An icon-only button needs an aria-label
Disabled and loading buttons are not focusable

components.name: Card
components.summary: Groups related content and actions about a single subject.
components.description: A surface that groups related content and actions about one subject. It has two variants — default (bordered) and elevated (shadow) — and is built from composable parts (header, title, description, content, footer), with slots for an Avatar in the header and a Button in the footer. Background, border, radius, and elevation are bound to semantic tokens.
whenToUse: Group related content and actions about a single subject
whenNotToUse: A bare list of text with no grouping

variant.elevated: Raised with a shadow (Elevation) instead of a border — for emphasis or layering over content.

dos: Keep one main call-to-action per card
donts: Don't nest cards more than one level deep
Don't make the whole card and an inner button separately clickable in conflicting ways

notes: Card renders a plain container with no implicit role — add role and aria-labelledby only if it's a meaningful region or is itself interactive
If the whole card is clickable, give it an accessible name and keyboard access
Don't rely on the shadow alone to convey meaning

components.name: Input
components.summary: Collects a single line of free-form text.
components.description: A single-line text field for free-form input. It comes in three sizes with default, focus, error, and disabled states, and an optional leading icon. Border, background, radius, and type are bound to semantic tokens; the focus state uses the focus-ring and border/focus tokens and the error state uses the danger tokens.
whenToUse: Collect a single line of free-form text — a name, email, or search query
whenNotToUse: Choosing from a fixed set of options — use Select or Radio

states.focus: Keyboard focus — shows the focus ring and the border shifts to border/focus.
states.error: Invalid input — border and ring use the danger token.
states.disabled: Non-interactive; reduced opacity and the field can't be edited.

dos: Always pair the field with a visible label
Show format hints as helper text
Reserve space for error text to avoid layout shift
donts: Don't use placeholder text as the only label
Don't validate on every keystroke before the first blur

keyboard: Tab moves focus to and from the field
notes: Every input needs a programmatically associated <label> — a placeholder is not a label
In the error state, set aria-invalid and link the message with aria-describedby
